correctness.rationale: The exp/log coordinate change is bijective over all fields of characteristic at least five; direct differentiation gives the sole bracket [t^2 d/dt,t^3 d/dt]=t^4 d/dt. Conjugation by the scalar multiplier has weights 1,2,3. Triangular central-series elimination removes each nonresonant coordinate; exactly the square/cube resonances remain at multipliers −1 and primitive cube roots. Each multiplier-fiber sum of class-size products equals q^3. The resulting k(G)=2q+4 gcd(3,q−1) gives the commuting-pair formula; the independently written checker exhaustively confirmed all claimed multiplier-resolved class sizes at q=5 and q=7. Finite checks do not prove the general case.

originality.rationale: Pálfy (1998) treats the unipotent Nottingham quotients rather than their scalar extension, and thus his class number does not determine the full-group multiplier fibers. Byszewski et al. (2020) treat torsion and automata, predominantly characteristic two, with no matching fourth-jet finite-field spectrum. Gorshkov (2022) studies abstract class-size restrictions without these finite substitution groups. Searches of mathematical literature and semantic published research records did not locate an equivalent full-group formula. The explicit multiplier-resolved orbit table, not the classical normal-form principle, is the assessed contribution. A differently indexed algebraic-group conjugacy enumeration remains a documented priority risk.

value.rationale: The first nonabelian finite substitution-jet group has a natural and intrinsic full conjugacy-class invariant. Its exact class-size spectrum identifies how scalar resonances govern conjugacy and centralizer geometry, and an arithmetic jump of eight classes as the field gains cubic roots of unity. This all-field structural classification is more than a small census or a textbook identity; unlike the unipotent subgroup enumeration it exposes how adding all invertible multipliers changes the symmetry types and commuting probability.
